# Built-in elements

The elements every `.zge` file can use. Components are made of them
(and of other components). See the [language guide](../language.md).

All elements have these properties:

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | length | in-out |
| `y` | length | in-out |
| `width` | length | in-out |
| `height` | length | in-out |
| `visible` | bool | in-out |
| `enabled` | bool | in-out |
| `opacity` | float | in-out |

In a layout, elements also take constraints, which the layout uses to
size them (`min-width`, `preferred-height`, ...), and in a GridLayout
their cell (`row`, `col`, `rowspan`, `colspan`):

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `min-width` | length | in-out |
| `max-width` | length | in-out |
| `preferred-width` | length | in-out |
| `min-height` | length | in-out |
| `max-height` | length | in-out |
| `preferred-height` | length | in-out |
| `horizontal-stretch` | float | in-out |
| `vertical-stretch` | float | in-out |
| `row`, `col` | int | in |
| `rowspan`, `colspan` | int | in |

All elements can also describe themselves to assistive technology
(screen readers). The standard widgets set these; set them on your
own components' elements:

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `accessible-role` | AccessibleRole | in-out |
| `accessible-label` | string | in-out |
| `accessible-description` | string | in-out |
| `accessible-value` | string | in-out |
| `accessible-value-minimum` | float | in-out |
| `accessible-value-maximum` | float | in-out |
| `accessible-value-step` | float | in-out |
| `accessible-checkable` | bool | in-out |
| `accessible-checked` | bool | in-out |
| `accessible-enabled` | bool | in-out |
| `accessible-placeholder-text` | string | in-out |
| `accessible-multiselectable` | bool | in-out |

and handle what assistive technology asks:

- `accessible-action-default()`
- `accessible-action-increment()`
- `accessible-action-decrement()`
- `accessible-action-set-value(string)`
- `accessible-action-select()`
- `accessible-action-set-selected(bool)`

## Window

The root of a component shown in a window. Its `width` and `height` are the window's initial size; `title` is for the backend. `fullscreen`, `maximized`, `minimized` and `always-on-top` say how the system shows it: set them to change it, and they follow when the user does (from the title bar, say), for backends that can (not KMS or the web; Wayland has no always-on-top). On phones and tablets, `safe-area-top`, `-left`, `-bottom` and `-right` are how far in from each edge the content is clear of the system's bars, notches and rounded corners, and `keyboard-height` how much of the bottom the on-screen keyboard covers (0 elsewhere). `input-activity` is called for every press, move, release, wheel turn, finger and key, whichever element takes it (an element dragging included): an inactivity timeout restarts on it.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | brush | in-out |
| `title` | string | in-out |
| `fullscreen` | bool | in-out |
| `maximized` | bool | in-out |
| `minimized` | bool | in-out |
| `always-on-top` | bool | in-out |
| `safe-area-top` | length | out (read-only) |
| `safe-area-left` | length | out (read-only) |
| `safe-area-bottom` | length | out (read-only) |
| `safe-area-right` | length | out (read-only) |
| `keyboard-height` | length | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `input-activity()`

## Empty

An element that draws nothing: a container for positioning children.

## Rectangle

A rectangle with an optional border and rounded corners. With `clip`, children are clipped to it (its corners rounded by `border-radius`, turned with it when rotated), and so is their input.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | brush | in-out |
| `border-color` | brush | in-out |
| `border-width` | length | in-out |
| `border-radius` | length | in-out |
| `clip` | bool | in-out |

## Text

A text. Without a `font-family`, it uses the window's default font. `wrap: word-wrap` breaks lines at the width. `letter-spacing` adds pixels after each character. With a `font-size-mode` other than `fixed`, the text is shown at the largest size up to `font-size` (down to `minimum-font-size`, 12px by default) that fits the element's width (`horizontal-fit`), height (`vertical-fit`) or both (`fit`).

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | in-out |
| `color` | brush | in-out |
| `font-size` | length | in-out |
| `font-family` | string | in-out |
| `font-weight` | int | in-out |
| `horizontal-alignment` | TextHorizontalAlignment | in-out |
| `vertical-alignment` | TextVerticalAlignment | in-out |
| `wrap` | TextWrap | in-out |
| `overflow` | TextOverflow | in-out |
| `letter-spacing` | length | in-out |
| `font-size-mode` | FontSizeMode | in-out |
| `minimum-font-size` | length | in-out |

## StyledText

Rich text: `text` in a Markdown subset, wrapped to the width and as tall as it needs (with `wrap: no-wrap`, lines break only where the text breaks them, cut at the edge). `horizontal-alignment` places each line across its width (tables stay at the left), `vertical-alignment` the text in its height. Inline: `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~struck~~`, `` `code` `` (on `code-background`, in `code-font-family`), `[links](url)` (in `link-color`; a click calls `link-clicked(url)`), `![images](url)`, `\` before a mark to write it. Blocks: paragraphs (a blank line between them), `#` to `######` headings, `-` bullets and `1.` numbered items (nested by two spaces), tables (`| a | b |` rows, a `| --- | --- |` line under the header; their lines and header in `code-background`), a line ending in two spaces or `\` breaks there. With `format: TextFormat.html`, an HTML subset instead: `p`, `div`, `br`, `h1` to `h6`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `b`, `strong`, `i`, `em`, `s`, `del`, `u`, `code`, `a href`, `img src` (`width`, `height`, `alt`), `table`, `tr`, `th`, `td`, entities; colors and fonts from `font` (`color`, `face`, `size`), `span`, `mark`, `big`, `small` and `style` attributes (`color`, `background-color`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `text-decoration`). Blocks take `align` or `text-align` (`left`, `center`, `right`, `justify`) over `horizontal-alignment`, inherited from a `div` or `center` around them; table cells too (Markdown's columns by `:---:` and `---:` under the header). `style-sheet` is CSS for the text (rules for tags, `.classes`, `#ids`, before HTML's own `style` elements; Markdown styled as the HTML it stands for). Images floated (`align=left`, `float: right`) sit beside the text, the lines after them going round. Images load as Image's `source-url` (a path, `file://`, `http(s)://`; relative ones from `base-url`, as a page's address: a directory ends with `/`) in the background, wrapping as words, no wider than a line; their `alt` text shows if they cannot be loaded. Bold is the family's weight 700; italics are slanted. `letter-spacing` adds pixels after each character; with a `font-size-mode` other than `fixed`, it is shown at the largest size up to `font-size` (down to `minimum-font-size`, headings, lists and tables with it) that fits, as Text's. With `selectable`, dragging over it selects text (`selected-text`, on `selection-color`; a double click selects a word, a triple click a paragraph), and Ctrl+C (Cmd+C) or `copy()` copies it; Ctrl+A or `select-all()` selects all.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | in-out |
| `color` | brush | in-out |
| `link-color` | brush | in-out |
| `code-background` | brush | in-out |
| `font-size` | length | in-out |
| `font-family` | string | in-out |
| `font-weight` | int | in-out |
| `code-font-family` | string | in-out |
| `base-url` | string | in-out |
| `style-sheet` | string | in-out |
| `letter-spacing` | length | in-out |
| `font-size-mode` | FontSizeMode | in-out |
| `minimum-font-size` | length | in-out |
| `wrap` | TextWrap | in-out |
| `horizontal-alignment` | TextHorizontalAlignment | in-out |
| `vertical-alignment` | TextVerticalAlignment | in-out |
| `format` | TextFormat | in-out |
| `selectable` | bool | in-out |
| `selection-color` | brush | in-out |
| `selected-text` | string | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `link-clicked(string)`

Functions: `copy()`, `select-all()`

## StackLayout

Shows one of its children: the one at `current-index` (the others are hidden: their visibility is the layout's), each filling it. It takes the largest of their sizes. `count` is how many there are.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `current-index` | int | in-out |
| `count` | int | out (read-only) |

## SwipeView

Its children side by side, each filling it, one shown: `current-index`; with `orientation: Orientation.vertical`, one above the other. A drag along them (mouse or finger) moves between them, settling on the nearest one (or the next, dragged a fifth of the way); setting `current-index` slides there. `count` is how many there are, `position` where it is (in pages). With `interactive: false`, only `current-index` moves it.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `current-index` | int | in-out |
| `count` | int | out (read-only) |
| `interactive` | bool | in-out |
| `position` | float | out (read-only) |
| `orientation` | Orientation | in-out |

## TreeState

Which rows of a tree show: the rows in order, with their depths (`levels`: 0 for the top ones, a child's one more than its parent's, right after it). `shown` is the rows shown (their indices: those whose parents are all expanded), `expanded` and `has-children` say it by row. `toggle(row)`, `expand(row)`, `collapse(row)`, `expand-all()`, `collapse-all()`; new rows start expanded if `initially-expanded`. std-widgets.zge's TreeView is made with it. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `levels` | [int] | in-out |
| `initially-expanded` | bool | in-out |
| `shown` | [int] | out (read-only) |
| `expanded` | [bool] | out (read-only) |
| `has-children` | [bool] | out (read-only) |

Functions: `toggle()`, `expand()`, `collapse()`, `expand-all()`, `collapse-all()`

## Selection

Which of `count` rows are selected, for views that let the user pick several: `selected` says it by row, `selected-rows` lists them. `select(row)` selects only that row (-1: none), `toggle(row)` adds or removes it, `extend-to(row)` selects the rows from the last one selected or toggled to `row` (Shift-click), in the order of `order` (the rows as shown, when not 0, 1, 2...); `set-selected(row, on)`, `select-all()`, `clear()`. `changed` is called when the selection changes. std-widgets.zge's StandardListView, StandardTableView and TreeView are made with it; use it in a ListView, TableView or GridView of your own rows. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `count` | int | in-out |
| `order` | [int] | in-out |
| `selected` | [bool] | out (read-only) |
| `selected-rows` | [int] | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `changed()`

Functions: `select()`, `toggle()`, `extend-to()`, `set-selected()`, `select-all()`, `clear()`

## FlowLayout

Its children at their preferred sizes, left to right, wrapping to the next row where they do not fit; rows and children `spacing` apart, `padding` inside. Its height is what the rows take at its width.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `spacing` | length | in-out |
| `padding` | length | in-out |

## ListLayout

The rows of the `for` in it, one under another, `spacing` apart, all as tall as `row-height` (0: the first row's preferred height) and as wide as it; with `variable-row-height`, each as tall as it prefers (rows not yet shown estimated at the mean of those that were). Only the rows within `visible-height` of `viewport-y` (a Flickable's) have instances, handed on to the rows coming into view as it scrolls (an instance's own state goes with it); without a `visible-height`, all rows. `sections` names each row's section: one starts where the name changes, under a `section-height` gap for its header; `section-names` and `section-ys` are the headers, `current-section` the section at the top of the view and `current-section-offset` where to pin its header (pushed up by the next). `column-widths` and `column-count` are the columns of its `TableRow`s. std-widgets.zge's ListView and TableView are made with it.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `viewport-y` | length | in-out |
| `visible-height` | length | in-out |
| `row-height` | length | in-out |
| `variable-row-height` | bool | in-out |
| `spacing` | length | in-out |
| `sections` | [string] | in-out |
| `section-height` | length | in-out |
| `column-widths` | [length] | in-out |
| `column-count` | int | in-out |
| `row-count` | int | out (read-only) |
| `current-section` | string | out (read-only) |
| `current-section-offset` | length | out (read-only) |
| `section-names` | [string] | out (read-only) |
| `section-ys` | [length] | out (read-only) |

## TableRow

A row of a table (the body of a `for` in a ListLayout, or a TableView): its children are its cells, one per column of the list, in order, as tall as the row. Its preferred height is its tallest cell's.

## SplitView

Its children (panes) side by side, or one above the other with `vertical`, with a handle between each two that the pointer drags to share the room (each pane stays within its minimum and maximum size). At first they share it by their preferred sizes. `handle-width` is the room a handle takes, `handle-color` its line.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `vertical` | bool | in-out |
| `handle-width` | length | in-out |
| `handle-color` | brush | in-out |

## StackView

Pages on top of each other: `push(Page)` (a component) shows one on top, sliding in from the right; `pop()` takes it off, sliding out; `clear()` goes back to the first. `initial-page` is the first one; one always stays. `depth` is how many there are, `busy` whether one is sliding.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `initial-page` | component | in-out |
| `depth` | int | out (read-only) |
| `busy` | bool | out (read-only) |

Functions: `push()`, `pop()`, `clear()`

## Shortcut

Keys that run something wherever the focus is: `activated` when `sequence` ("Ctrl+S", "Ctrl+Shift+Z", "Alt+Left", "Escape") is pressed and the focused element does not take it (Ctrl+C in a text field copies there). `Ctrl` is Command on macOS. Application-wide, while `enabled`. Menu bar items' shortcuts are made with it. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | string | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `activated()`

## PinchArea

Scaled and turned by two fingers (or a trackpad's pinch and rotation): while `active`, `pinch-scale` (1 at the start) and `pinch-rotation` (degrees, clockwise) follow the gesture, about `center-x`, `center-y`; `started`, `updated` and `finished` mark it. One finger still works as the mouse in it. Draws nothing.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `active` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `pinch-scale` | float | out (read-only) |
| `pinch-rotation` | float | out (read-only) |
| `center-x` | length | out (read-only) |
| `center-y` | length | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `started()`
- `updated()`
- `finished()`

## SwipeArea

Reports a quick drag over it (the mouse or a finger): `swiped(direction)` once it went `distance` (40 px) mostly one way (`SwipeDirection.left`, `right`, `up`, `down`). While dragging, `swiping` and `offset-x`, `offset-y` follow it. A press that does not move goes to what is in it. Draws nothing.

|---|---|---|
| `distance` | length | in-out |
| `swiping` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `offset-x` | length | out (read-only) |
| `offset-y` | length | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `swiped(SwipeDirection)`

## DragArea

Dragged by the pointer: a press moved past a few pixels starts dragging its `kind` and `data` (strings) to a DropArea that `accepts` the kind. It draws nothing: bind what shows the drag to `dragging` and `offset-x`, `offset-y` (the pointer since the press). `started` at the start, `finished(dropped)` at the end (`true` if dropped on a DropArea); `clicked` for a press released without dragging. Escape cancels.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | in-out |
| `data` | string | in-out |
| `dragging` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `offset-x` | length | out (read-only) |
| `offset-y` | length | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `started()`
- `finished(bool)`
- `clicked()`

Takes what a DragArea drops on it, of the kind it `accepts` ("": any): `contains-drag` while one is over it (its `drag-kind`, `drag-data`, and the pointer at `drag-x`, `drag-y`), `entered` and `exited`, then `dropped(data)`. The topmost one under the pointer takes it.

| `drag-y` | length | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `dropped(string)`

## TouchArea

Reports pointer input in its area: `clicked` after a press and release inside it, `moved` while the pointer moves over it or is pressed, `right-clicked` after the right button (to open a context menu). A second click within `double-click-interval` (400 ms) of the first, close to it, calls `double-clicked` instead of `clicked` when that has a handler (as Qt's MouseArea). `pointer-event(event)` tells every press and release of any button (`event.kind`: `PointerEventKind.down`, `up`), move over it or while pressed (`move`), and a press taken away by another element dragging (`cancel`), with `event.button` (`PointerEventButton.left`, `right`, `middle`, `other`) and `event.modifiers`. `modifiers` are the keys held at the press (`modifiers.shift` for a Shift-click).

| `mouse-y` | length | out (read-only) |
| `pressed-x` | length | out (read-only) |
| `pressed-y` | length | out (read-only) |
| `modifiers` | KeyboardModifiers | out (read-only) |
| `double-click-interval` | duration | in-out |

## Flickable

Scrolls its children (the viewport) by dragging or the mouse wheel. Taps still reach the children. With `snap-x` or `snap-y`, scrolling settles on multiples of it; with `snap-to-items`, where the content says (a ListLayout's rows, under its pinned section header, and its columns when they have widths); either way on the content's ends too, and the wheel moves by one snap position. `scroll-to-top()` and `scroll-to-bottom()` scroll there; after `scroll-to-bottom()` it keeps at the bottom as the content's height changes (rows measured, rows added) until scrolled elsewhere. With `overscroll` (the default), content dragged past its ends follows less and less and springs back when let go, and a flick into an end overshoots it and settles. `settle()` settles on the nearest snap position, within the ends (what a scroll bar let go calls).

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `viewport-x` | length | in-out |
| `viewport-y` | length | in-out |
| `viewport-width` | length | in-out |
| `viewport-height` | length | in-out |
| `interactive` | bool | in-out |
| `snap-x` | length | in-out |
| `snap-y` | length | in-out |
| `snap-to-items` | bool | in-out |
| `overscroll` | bool | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `flicked()`

Functions: `scroll-to-top()`, `scroll-to-bottom()`, `settle()`

## StateMachine

A state machine (statechart), with SCXML's semantics; not drawn. `event name(types);` declares an event, sent by calling it: `machine.name(args)`. `state name { ... }` declares a state (the first, or the one named by `initial name;`, is entered first); in it, `entered => { }` and `exited => { }` run on entering and leaving it, `on event(params) when guard => target { actions }` is a transition (the guard, the target and the actions each optional: without a target it neither leaves nor enters a state), `after duration ...` one taken once the state has been active that long. States can hold states (`initial name;` inside one names the first, `history;` or `history deep;` makes it remember where it was, entered back by targeting `name.history`); a state's transitions apply to those inside it, after their own, and a state is named by its name (looked for near the transition first) or, where that is ambiguous, its path (`menu.detail`). `parallel name { ... }` holds regions all active together (`<region>-state` reads each one's state); `final name;` is a final state, entering it raises `done.<parent>` (`on done.x => ...`; a parallel state is done when all its regions are); `when guard => target` is taken as soon as its guard holds (checked on entry and after each event). Events are processed one at a time to completion, those its own actions send before those from outside; the first enabled transition in order is taken; exit actions run before the transition's actions, before entry actions. `active(name)` says whether a state is active (one with states inside, with any of them), `current` is the innermost active state's path (`on/menu/detail`; "" when stopped), `state` is it as a value of the enum `<Id>State` made for the machine. It runs from when its component is made unless `running` is false; `start()` and `stop()` start it again and stop it (exit actions run).

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `running` | bool | in-out |
| `current` | string | out (read-only) |

Functions: `start()`, `stop()`

## Timer

Calls `triggered` every `interval` while `running`. `start()` and `stop()` set and clear `running`; `restart()` runs it from now, the next `triggered` a whole `interval` away. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `interval` | duration | in-out |
| `running` | bool | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `triggered()`

Functions: `start()`, `stop()`, `restart()`

## Audio

Plays `source` while `playing`: set it, or call `play()` and `stop()`. `play()` starts the sound again from the start; with `voices` above 1 it plays over the voices still playing, up to that many (the oldest is cut). Voices rise over `fade-in` and, when stopped, fall over `fade-out`; a new `source` fades in while the old one fades out. `position` follows playback, and setting it seeks. `finished` is called when playback ends by itself (never while `loop`ing). Silent where the platform has no audio output. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | audio | in-out |
| `playing` | bool | in-out |
| `paused` | bool | in-out |
| `loop` | bool | in-out |
| `volume` | float | in-out |
| `pan` | float | in-out |
| `speed` | float | in-out |
| `voices` | int | in-out |
| `fade-in` | duration | in-out |
| `fade-out` | duration | in-out |
| `position` | duration | in-out |
| `duration` | duration | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `finished()`

Functions: `play()`, `stop()`

## Video

Plays a video and shows it like an `Image` (`image-fit`; the video's size is its preferred size): `source` is embedded at build time (`@video-url("intro.png")`), `source-file` is a file read while playing (and wins when set). Animated PNG plays everywhere; other formats (MP4, ...) where the platform decodes them. It shows the first frame until `playing` is set (or `play()` is called); `stop()` goes back to the start. `position` follows playback, and setting it seeks; `finished` is called when playback ends by itself, keeping the last frame. The soundtrack plays through the mixer at `volume`.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | video | in-out |
| `source-file` | string | in-out |
| `playing` | bool | in-out |
| `paused` | bool | in-out |
| `loop` | bool | in-out |
| `volume` | float | in-out |
| `position` | duration | in-out |
| `duration` | duration | out (read-only) |
| `image-fit` | ImageFit | in-out |
| `image-rendering` | ImageRendering | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `finished()`

Functions: `play()`, `stop()`

## View3D

A 3D scene: its `Node`, `Model`, `PerspectiveCamera`, `DirectionalLight` and `PointLight` children, drawn over `background` (transparent by default) with `ambient` light everywhere, times `ambient-brightness` (1 by default). Y points up and the camera looks along -z. Without a camera it is seen from 4 units in front of the middle; without lights, lit from the upper left. Drawn on the CPU into an image (twice the element's size, smoothed), kept while the scene is the same: suited to small scenes. Other children are drawn over it as usual.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | color | in-out |
| `ambient` | color | in-out |
| `ambient-brightness` | float | in-out |

## Model

A shape in a `View3D`: a `mesh` (`cube`, `sphere` or `plane`, each 1 unit across, centered; the plane facing +z), sized by `size-x`, `size-y` and `size-z`, at `position-x`, `position-y` and `position-z`, turned by `yaw` (about y), then `pitch` (about x), then `roll` (about z), in degrees. Its material: `color`, multiplied by `texture` if set, `metallic` (0 to 1) and `roughness` (0 shiny to 1 matte, 0.5 by default). With a `source` (`@model-url("ship.glb")`, a glTF 2.0 binary file embedded at build time), it shows that model's meshes, sized and placed the same way, in the model's own materials tinted by `color`. A click on it (the nearest model under the pointer) calls `clicked`. Nodes inside a model move and turn with it (not sized with it).

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `position-x` | float | in-out |
| `position-y` | float | in-out |
| `position-z` | float | in-out |
| `pitch` | float | in-out |
| `yaw` | float | in-out |
| `roll` | float | in-out |
| `mesh` | Mesh | in-out |
| `source` | model3d | in-out |
| `size-x` | float | in-out |
| `size-y` | float | in-out |
| `size-z` | float | in-out |
| `color` | color | in-out |
| `metallic` | float | in-out |
| `roughness` | float | in-out |
| `texture` | image | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `clicked()`

## Node

A group in a `View3D`, drawing nothing: the nodes inside it (models, cameras, lights, other nodes) move and turn with it. At `position-x`, `position-y` and `position-z`, turned by `yaw`, `pitch` and `roll` (degrees). A camera inside a turning node goes round what it looks at.

| `position-z` | float | in-out |
| `pitch` | float | in-out |
| `yaw` | float | in-out |
| `roll` | float | in-out |

## PerspectiveCamera

Where a `View3D` is seen from: at `position-x`, `position-y` and `position-z` (0, 0, 4 by default), looking along its -z axis turned by `yaw`, `pitch` and `roll`, with a vertical `field-of-view` in degrees (45 by default). The first camera counts.

| `roll` | float | in-out |
| `field-of-view` | float | in-out |

## DirectionalLight

Light from far away in a `View3D`, as from the sun: shining along its -z axis turned by `yaw` and `pitch` (by default, away from the default camera), in `color`, times `brightness` (1 by default).

Takes no child elements.

## PointLight

Light from a point in a `View3D`, as from a bulb: at `position-x`, `position-y` and `position-z`, in `color`, times `brightness` (1 by default), half as bright `range` units away (10 by default).

## WebView

A web page: `url` loads (and follows the page's links and redirects), or `html` shows that text (and wins when set). `title`, `loading`, `can-go-back` and `can-go-forward` follow the page; `back()`, `forward()`, `reload()` and `stop()` act on it; `finished` is called when a page has loaded, `failed` when it could not (`error` says why). `run-javascript(code)` runs code in the page: `javascript-finished(result)` then, as text, or `javascript-failed(error)`. `set-cookie(url, cookie)` stores a cookie for `url` as a server's `Set-Cookie` header would (`"session=abc; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly"`): a session the app holds natively, handed over, HttpOnly included; pages loaded after it wait until it is stored (not on the web, where an `<iframe>` cannot be given one). A native view placed over the element: it shows above everything (popups too), without rotation, opacity or effects, and is not clipped by scroll views. `available` tells whether the platform has web views: macOS and Windows (native and SDL3 backends; Windows needs the WebView2 runtime), Linux with X11 (native and SDL3 backends, with WebKitGTK installed), iOS and the web (an `<iframe>`, where other sites cannot be scripted or navigated); not on Wayland or KMS.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | in-out |
| `html` | string | in-out |
| `title` | string | out (read-only) |
| `loading` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `can-go-back` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `can-go-forward` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `error` | string | out (read-only) |
| `available` | bool | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `finished()`
- `failed()`
- `javascript-finished(string)`
- `javascript-failed(string)`

Functions: `back()`, `forward()`, `reload()`, `stop()`, `run-javascript()`, `set-cookie()`

## Camera

The camera's picture, shown like an `Image` (`image-fit`) while `active` (the camera runs while one is; the first time, the platform may ask the user). `take-picture()` keeps the frame shown as `picture` (an image to show elsewhere) and calls `picture-taken`; `save-picture(path)` writes it as a PNG file. `available` tells whether there is a camera (with the SDL3 backend: macOS, Windows, Linux; with the native macOS one).

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `active` | bool | in-out |
| `available` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `picture` | image | out (read-only) |
| `image-fit` | ImageFit | in-out |
| `image-rendering` | ImageRendering | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `picture-taken()`

Functions: `take-picture()`, `save-picture()`

## Accelerometer

The device's acceleration while `active`: `x`, `y` and `z` in m/s², gravity included (lying face up: 0, 0, 9.81), with x to the right, y up and z out of the screen, the device held upright. `reading-changed` is called at each reading, at most `data-rate` times a second (0, the default: as they come). `available` tells whether there is one (in browsers: the API, which computers have without the sensor). On iOS, the browser asks the user first, at the next tap. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |

| `active` | bool | in-out |

| `data-rate` | int | in-out |
| `x` | float | out (read-only) |
| `y` | float | out (read-only) |
| `z` | float | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `reading-changed()`

## Gyroscope

How fast the device turns while `active`: about `x`, `y` and `z` (the `Accelerometer`'s axes) in degrees a second, counterclockwise looking down the axis. `reading-changed`, `data-rate` and `available` as the `Accelerometer`'s. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

- `reading-changed()`

## Compass

Where the device points while `active`: `azimuth` in degrees clockwise from magnetic north (0 to 360), and `calibration-level` (0 to 1). `reading-changed`, `data-rate` and `available` as the `Accelerometer`'s. Not drawn.

## OrientationSensor

Which side of the device is up while `active`: `orientation` is `DeviceOrientation.top-up` (upright), `top-down`, `left-up`, `right-up`, `face-up`, `face-down`, or `unknown` until known. Worked out from the accelerometer where the platform tells no orientation itself. `reading-changed`, `data-rate` and `available` as the `Accelerometer`'s. Not drawn.

## MapView

A map of web tiles centered on `latitude`, `longitude` at `zoom` (0: the world in one tile; each step doubles the scale; within `minimum-zoom` and `maximum-zoom`, 0 and 19 by default), Web Mercator. Tiles come from `tile-url`, a template whose `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}` are filled in (OpenStreetMap's by default; `file://` works too; empty: none), loaded in the background and kept in memory and for a week in the application's cache; lower zoom levels stand in while they come. On screens of 1.5 pixels a point or more (with `high-density`, the default), the next zoom level's tiles show at half their size, sharp, or with a `{r}` in the template (filled with `@2x`), the server's own. `attribution` shows in the bottom right corner (OpenStreetMap's by default: its terms ask for it), and `user-agent` is said to tile servers (by default the application's name, which OpenStreetMap's policy asks for). While `interactive` (the default), dragging pans, the wheel and pinching zoom, and a double click zooms in; a click calls `clicked(latitude, longitude)`. `zoom-in()` and `zoom-out()` go a step. `MapItem` and `MapPolyline` children stand at coordinates; other children are placed as usual, over the map. On the web, tiles come through the browser (the tile server must allow it, as OpenStreetMap's does); none from the network on microcontrollers.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | float | in-out |
| `longitude` | float | in-out |
| `zoom` | float | in-out |
| `minimum-zoom` | float | in-out |
| `maximum-zoom` | float | in-out |
| `tile-url` | string | in-out |
| `attribution` | string | in-out |
| `user-agent` | string | in-out |
| `interactive` | bool | in-out |
| `high-density` | bool | in-out |
| `background` | brush | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `clicked(float, float)`

Functions: `zoom-in()`, `zoom-out()`

In a `MapView`: stands at `latitude`, `longitude`, the point `anchor-x`, `anchor-y` of it (fractions of its size; 0.5, 0.5, the default, its middle; 0.5, 1 its bottom middle, for a pin) on the coordinate. Give it a size; its children are what shows there (a marker: any elements).

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | float | in-out |
| `longitude` | float | in-out |
| `anchor-x` | float | in-out |
| `anchor-y` | float | in-out |

## MapPolyline

In a `MapView`: a line through `coordinates`, given as latitude, longitude, latitude, longitude... (`[45.46, 9.19, 45.07, 7.69]`), in `stroke` (blue by default), `stroke-width` wide (3px by default). `closed`, it goes back to the start: an outline, filled with `fill`.

Takes no child elements.

Not drawn.

## Microphone

The microphone: while `active`, `level` follows how loud it is (0 to 1, falling off slowly), for a meter. `record()` keeps what it hears (it runs meanwhile, `active` or not; `recording`, `duration` so far) until `stop()`: then `recorded` is that sound, for an `Audio` element to play, and `finished` is called; `save-recording(path)` writes it as a WAV file. Recordings are mono, at most ten minutes. The first time, the platform may ask the user. `available` tells whether there is a microphone input (with the SDL3 backend: macOS, Windows, Linux; with the native macOS one). Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

## Connections

Handlers for another element's callbacks: `Connections { target: list; selected(i) => { ... } }`. They are added to the element's own handlers (which run first) and run while `enabled`. `target` is an element's id, `root`, `parent` or a global. A single one can also be written on any element: `list.selected(i) => { ... }`. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |

| `enabled` | bool | in-out |

## Loader

Shows the component `source` names (a component's name, or a `component` property), created at run time, while `active`: its root fills the loader. Another source replaces it. The loader's other bindings are passed to the instance's input properties of the same name and type (`Loader { source: delegate; data: row; index: i; }`); a component without one is logged. `loaded` says whether an instance is shown.

Takes no child elements.

The platform's file dialog: `open()` shows it, to open a file (`mode: open-file`), several (`open-files`), a folder (`open-folder`) or a file to save (`save-file`). `filter` limits the files shown, as in Qt: `"Images (*.png *.jpg);;All files (*)"`. `folder` is where it starts, `file-name` the name suggested to save. The answer is `selected-file` (and all of them, `selected-files`), then `accepted`; or `rejected` if cancelled. Where there are no file dialogs (the web, microcontrollers), it is always rejected. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

## HttpRequest

A request over HTTP or HTTPS, made by `send()` (`abort()` drops it): to `url`, with `method` (`get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`), `headers` ("Name: value" each) and a `body`. It runs in the background (`loading` meanwhile); the answer is `status` and `response`, then `finished` (whatever the status), or if there was none (no network, a bad address), `error` says why, then `failed`. `json-get`, `json-number` and `json-count` read JSON answers. Without threads (the web, microcontrollers), requests fail. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | in-out |
| `method` | HttpMethod | in-out |
| `headers` | [string] | in-out |
| `body` | string | in-out |
| `loading` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `status` | int | out (read-only) |
| `response` | string | out (read-only) |
| `error` | string | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `finished()`
- `failed()`

Functions: `send()`, `abort()`

## Canvas

2D drawing from code, as QML's Canvas and HTML's: the `paint` handler calls the drawing functions, in the canvas's coordinates (lengths; angles in degrees, clockwise). Paths: `begin-path()`, `move-to(x, y)`, `line-to(x, y)`, `quadratic-curve-to(cx, cy, x, y)`, `bezier-curve-to(c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, x, y)`, `arc(x, y, radius, start-angle, end-angle, anticlockwise)` (from 3 o'clock), `rect(x, y, w, h)`, `rounded-rect(x, y, w, h, radius)`, `ellipse(x, y, w, h)`, `close-path()`, then `fill()` (in `fill-style`), `stroke()` (in `stroke-style`, `line-width` wide) or `clip()`. Also `fill-rect`, `stroke-rect`, `clear-rect` (of the whole canvas), `fill-text(text, x, y)` (on its baseline, in `font-size`, `font-family`, `font-weight`, aligned by `text-align`), `draw-image(image, x, y, w, h)`; `translate(x, y)`, `rotate(degrees)`, `scale(sx, sy)`, `reset-transform()`; `save()` and `restore()` (the transform, the styles and the clip). `global-alpha` fades what follows. Each paint starts from an empty canvas; `paint` runs again when the canvas is resized, when a property it read changes, and on `request-paint()`.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `fill-style` | brush | in-out |
| `stroke-style` | brush | in-out |
| `line-width` | length | in-out |
| `global-alpha` | float | in-out |
| `font-size` | length | in-out |
| `font-family` | string | in-out |
| `font-weight` | int | in-out |
| `text-align` | TextHorizontalAlignment | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `paint()`

Functions: `request-paint()`, `begin-path()`, `close-path()`, `move-to()`, `line-to()`, `quadratic-curve-to()`, `bezier-curve-to()`, `arc()`, `rect()`, `rounded-rect()`, `ellipse()`, `fill()`, `stroke()`, `clip()`, `fill-rect()`, `stroke-rect()`, `clear-rect()`, `fill-text()`, `draw-image()`, `save()`, `restore()`, `translate()`, `rotate()`, `scale()`, `reset-transform()`

## LineChart

The `values` as a line from left to right, within the element: `color` and `line-width`, an area down to 0 with `fill`, dots with `point-size`. It shows the values from `minimum` to `maximum`, or if those are not set, a range around the values and 0 rounded so that `grid-lines` lines (drawn in `grid-color`) fall on round values: `shown-minimum` and `shown-maximum` tell which, to label them. The point nearest the pointer is `hovered-index` (-1: none), and a click on it calls `clicked(index)`. Several charts with the same `minimum` and `maximum` stacked show several series.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | [float] | in-out |
| `minimum` | float | in-out |
| `maximum` | float | in-out |
| `color` | brush | in-out |
| `line-width` | length | in-out |
| `fill` | brush | in-out |
| `point-size` | length | in-out |
| `grid-lines` | int | in-out |
| `grid-color` | brush | in-out |
| `shown-minimum` | float | out (read-only) |
| `shown-maximum` | float | out (read-only) |
| `hovered-index` | int | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `clicked(int)`

## BarChart

The `values` as bars side by side, up from 0 (down if negative), within the element: in `colors` (repeated; ten colors by default), `spacing` the part of each bar's place left between them, with rounded corners (`border-radius`). The range shown, grid lines, `hovered-index` and `clicked(index)` are as in `LineChart`.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | [float] | in-out |
| `colors` | [color] | in-out |
| `minimum` | float | in-out |
| `maximum` | float | in-out |
| `spacing` | float | in-out |
| `border-radius` | length | in-out |
| `grid-lines` | int | in-out |
| `grid-color` | brush | in-out |
| `shown-minimum` | float | out (read-only) |
| `shown-maximum` | float | out (read-only) |
| `hovered-index` | int | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `clicked(int)`

## PieChart

The `values` as slices of a circle, clockwise from the top, each its part of their sum (negative values count as none), in `colors` (repeated; ten colors by default); a ring with `hole`, the part of the radius left empty (0 to 0.95). The slice under the pointer is `hovered-index` (-1: none), and a click on it calls `clicked(index)`.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | [float] | in-out |
| `colors` | [color] | in-out |
| `hole` | float | in-out |
| `hovered-index` | int | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `clicked(int)`

## KeyboardInput

What an on-screen keyboard needs (`VirtualKeyboard` is one): `active` while a text input that can be edited has the keyboard focus (`multi-line` and `password` tell what kind), `send(text)` types a character or a key (`Key.Backspace`, `Key.Return`, ...) into it, and `dismiss()` takes its focus away. Clicks on the keyboard leave the focus where it is. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `active` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `multi-line` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `password` | bool | out (read-only) |

Functions: `send()`, `dismiss()`

## Settings

Properties kept from one run of the application to the next: a component that inherits `Settings` has its declared properties (int, float, bool, string, length, duration, color) saved, under `category`, in `settings.ini` in the application's configuration folder (`StandardPaths`' `app-config`), or in `file`. With `format: registry`, on Windows they go in the registry instead, as QSettings does: under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\<app>`, or the key given as `file` (under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER`), a key per category; elsewhere `registry` is an INI file still. Saved values replace the defaults once the component and its users are set up, so properties linked to them with `<=>` take them too. Changes are written a moment later, and when it goes. Where there are no files (the web, microcontrollers), they last as long as the application. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `category` | string | in-out |
| `file` | string | in-out |
| `format` | SettingsFormat | in-out |

## StandardPaths

Where things go on this system: the user's `home`, `desktop`, `documents`, `downloads`, `pictures`, `music` and `videos` folders, `temp`, and the application's own folders for configuration (`app-config`), data (`app-data`) and caches (`app-cache`), named after the application (`zigulee.core.paths.setApplicationName`, else the executable's name). Empty where there is none (an iOS app has no desktop; the web and microcontrollers have no files). Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `home` | string | out (read-only) |
| `desktop` | string | out (read-only) |
| `documents` | string | out (read-only) |
| `downloads` | string | out (read-only) |
| `pictures` | string | out (read-only) |
| `music` | string | out (read-only) |
| `videos` | string | out (read-only) |
| `temp` | string | out (read-only) |
| `app-config` | string | out (read-only) |
| `app-data` | string | out (read-only) |
| `app-cache` | string | out (read-only) |

## SystemTrayIcon

An icon in the system tray (on the right of macOS's menu bar, in Windows' notification area), shown while `visible`: its `icon` (macOS shows `tooltip` as its title when there is none) and `tooltip`. Its `PlatformMenuItem` children are its menu, opened by a click; without any, a click calls `activated`. `available` tells whether the platform has a tray (not on Linux yet, the web, mobile or microcontrollers). Not drawn.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `icon` | image | in-out |
| `tooltip` | string | in-out |
| `available` | bool | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `activated()`

## Notification

A desktop notification: `send()` shows `title` and `body` (each call another one), and a click on it calls `clicked`. `available` tells whether the platform shows them (macOS, from an application bundle; Windows; Linux desktops); elsewhere `send()` only logs. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | in-out |
| `body` | string | in-out |
| `available` | bool | out (read-only) |

Callbacks:

- `clicked()`

Functions: `send()`

## PlatformMenu

A menu of the platform's menu bar (macOS's, at the top of the screen), with `PlatformMenuItem` children; `native` tells whether there is one (elsewhere it does nothing, and menus belong in the window). `MenuBarItem` makes one. Not drawn.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | in-out |
| `native` | bool | out (read-only) |

## PlatformMenuItem

An entry of a `PlatformMenu`: `text`, a `shortcut` ("Ctrl+S", ⌘S on macOS), `checked`, `enabled`, or a `separator` line; `activated` when chosen. `level` nests it: the entries right after one, a level deeper, are its submenu. Not drawn.

Takes no child elements.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | in-out |
| `shortcut` | string | in-out |
| `checked` | bool | in-out |
| `enabled` | bool | in-out |
| `separator` | bool | in-out |
| `level` | int | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `activated()`

## PopupWindow

Content shown above everything else with `show()`, at its position relative to its parent. Closed with `close()` or, depending on `close-policy`, a click (a click on what it shows past its bounds, a menu's submenu, is a click inside). `window-x` and `window-y` are where it was shown in the window, `window-width` and `window-height` the window's size then. While closed, with an `edge-margin` (0 by default: none), a drag the `open-swipe` way (`SwipeDirection.right` by default) begun that close to the window's opposite edge pulls it out: `edge-dragged(distance)` as it goes, `edge-released(distance, speed)` at the end (speed in pixels a second, that way); a press there that does not go that way goes to what is under it.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `close-policy` | PopupClosePolicy | in-out |
| `is-open` | bool | out (read-only) |
| `input-transparent` | bool | in-out |
| `fit-in-window` | bool | in-out |
| `fill-window` | bool | in-out |
| `window-x` | length | out (read-only) |
| `window-y` | length | out (read-only) |
| `window-width` | length | out (read-only) |
| `window-height` | length | out (read-only) |
| `open-swipe` | SwipeDirection | in-out |
| `edge-margin` | length | in-out |

Callbacks:

- `edge-dragged(length)`
- `edge-released(length, float)`

Functions: `show()`, `close()`

## GridLayout

Places its children in a grid: in `Row` elements, or by their `row` and `col` properties. Cells can take `rowspan` and `colspan`.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `spacing` | length | in-out |
| `padding` | length | in-out |
| `padding-left` | length | in-out |
| `padding-right` | length | in-out |
| `padding-top` | length | in-out |
| `padding-bottom` | length | in-out |

## HorizontalLayout

Places its children side by side, sized by their constraints and stretch factors.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `spacing` | length | in-out |
| `padding` | length | in-out |
| `padding-left` | length | in-out |
| `padding-right` | length | in-out |
| `padding-top` | length | in-out |
| `padding-bottom` | length | in-out |
| `alignment` | LayoutAlignment | in-out |

## VerticalLayout

Places its children one below the other, sized by their constraints and stretch factors.

| Property | Type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `spacing` | length | in-out |
| `padding` | length | in-out |
| `padding-left` | length | in-out |
| `padding-right` | length | in-out |
| `padding-top` | length | in-out |
| `padding-bottom` | length | in-out |
| `alignment` | LayoutAlignment | in-out |
